brief.title: Design the evaluation
brief.plain_summary: Turn a question into an evaluation plan: arms, metrics, runs per arm, scoring and draft pass marks for a person to approve.
brief.outcome: A plan, one arm noun per arm and draft pass marks, or no_change when an existing evaluation already answers the question.

question.description: Pin of a noun stating the question and the decision it informs.

prior_evaluations.description: Pins of earlier evaluation reports on the same question.

output_store.description: Store for the produced nouns. The default is a placeholder; use the store your owner assigned.

output_contract.delivery: Write produced nouns surface_only under your own authenticated surface, which is the requester's assigned surface, so the requester and that surface's reviewers can read them. Never use public_commons or allowlist other surfaces. Return every produced noun's pin in output.artifacts; add its value when the requester asks for inline delivery.

outcome_meanings.plan_ready: The declared nouns were produced and every deterministic acceptance check passed.
outcome_meanings.no_change: The evidence does not justify producing or changing anything. Say why.
outcome_meanings.unknown: The question could not be answered with the permitted inputs. List what is missing and what would resolve it.
outcome_meanings.blocked: A required input, permission or capability is missing. Ask one precise question.

acceptance_checks.check: The plan validates against template.evaluation-plan's schema.
Exactly one arm has role baseline, and runs_per_arm is at least 2.
Every arm noun names an exact model identifier and a settings source.
The draft pass marks reference only arms and metrics in the plan.
The arms and metrics can actually answer the stated question.

creates.nouns: The worker writes the nouns listed in output_contract.produces and returns their pins.
creates.verbs: The worker proposes follow-up verbs in output.proposed_verbs, such as a breakdown into smaller verbs or a research follow-up, with the pins they need. Proposals are never enqueued by the worker; an authorized requester enqueues the ones worth doing.

required: Verify the pins. State the question and the decision it informs in one sentence each.
Define a baseline and the fewest arms that answer the question, one change per arm where possible.
Pick metrics from the method's menu and say why each matters to the decision.
Draft pass marks with thresholds; they stay drafts until a person commits them.
Estimate cost per arm from dated prices and label it an estimate.
Propose a freeze-set verb, a commit-pass-marks verb for a person, and two run-arm verbs per arm to follow them.
Return follow-up work the results justify as proposed_verbs and nouns worth creating later as proposed_nouns. Never enqueue them yourself; an authorized requester decides which to run.
